source_text: De recens baptizatis Τοῦ μακαρίου Ἀμφιλοχίου ἐπισκόπου Ἰκονίου περὶ τῶν νεοφωτίστων καὶ εἰς τὴν ἀνάστασιν τοῦ σωτῆρος ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ. Ὁπόταν τὸ σκυθρωπὸν τοῦ χειμῶνος ὁ τοῦ ἔαρος καιρὸς διαδέξηται, ποικίλοι ὄρνεις ἀνὰ τὸν αἰθέρα πετόμενοι μελιφώνοις ᾠδαῖς τὸ ἡδὺ τοῦ καιροῦ τοῖς ἀνθρώποις σημαίνουσιν· τότε καὶ χελιδόνες ἡδύλαλοι ὀξείᾳ πτήσει τὸν ἀέρα τέμνουσαι καὶ τὰς τῶν ἀνθρώπων κεφαλὰς παρατρέχουσαι δίκην ἄνθους τὴν οἰκείαν κλαγγὴν τοῖς ὠσὶν τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἐμβάλλουσιν. Τότε ἔστιν ἰδεῖν καθαρὸν τὸν ἀέρα καὶ νήνεμον καὶ τὰς τῶν ἀνθρώπων ὄψεις φαιδρὰς εἰς μίμημα τῆς γαλήνης μεταρρυθμιζομένας· καὶ γὰρ ὀρνέων φθογγαὶ τέρπουσιν ἀκοὴν καὶ ἀὴρ καθαρὸς φαιδρύνει τὸ ὄμμα καὶ ποικίλων ἀνθῶν στιλβότης ἡδύνει τὴν ὅρασιν καὶ ἡ πολυμιγὴς πνοὴ τῶν βοτανῶν ἀνακτᾶται τὴν ὄσφρησιν. Καὶ ταύτην μὲν τὴν τερπνότητα τοῖς ἀνθρώποις παρέχει, ἀγαπητοί, τὸ ἐπίγειον καὶ ἐπίκηρον ἔαρ· τὸ δὲ θεῖον καὶ ἀκήρατον ἔαρ ἡμῶν Χριστὸς τὸν λειμῶνα τῆς ἐκκλησίας ἴων καὶ ῥόδων καὶ κρίνων πνευματικῶν πυκάσας τῇ πίστει φαιδρύνει τὴν ὅρασιν καὶ ἀρωμά των θείων τὴν δεξαμενὴν τῆς καρδίας ἡμῶν πληροῖ. Τίς γὰρ τῶν πιστῶν νῦν οὐκ εὐφραίνεται; Τίς δὲ νῦν οὐκ ἀγάλλεται, ὅτε ὁρᾷ τοὺς νεοφωτίστους ἐν εἰκόνι κρίνων λαμ προῖς τοῖς κάλυξιν τῶν πέπλων καταλάμποντας καὶ ἐν μέσῃ τῇ καρδίᾳ κεκτημένους τὴν χρυσαυγοῦσαν πίστιν; Ἐνταῦθα εὑρή σεις, ἀγαπητέ, ὀφθαλμοῖς καρδίας ἀτενίσας ἴου δίκην βαθυτάτου τὴν τῶν πιστῶν καρδίαν αἵματι Ἰησοῦ πορφυρίζουσαν· τὸ γὰρ φλογόφυλλον ῥόδον ἐκ τῆς παρθένου Μαρίας ἀφθόρως ἐξήνθη σεν. Ποῖος λειμὼν τοιαύτην εὐωδίαν κέκτηται οἵαν ὁ ἡμέτερος λειμὼν τὴν τοῦ πνεύματος ἀρωματίζουσαν χάριν; Ὄσφρησαι τὸν νεοφώτιστον καὶ εὑρήσεις ἐν αὐτῷ τὴν τοῦ πνεύματος ἀθάνατον εὐωδίαν, λέγω δὴ τὸ τοῦ οὐρανίου χρίσματος μύρον. Ὧδε τῶν πατέρων οἱ φοίνικες τοῖς βαΐοις τῆς νίκης κατεστεμμένοι γλυκυτέρους τοὺς καρποὺς τῆς ἀγάπης κυπρίζουσιν· ὧδε τὰ καλλί φθογγα ὄρνεα τῶν ψαλμῳδῶν ὁμοφώνως τῷ θεῷ τοὺς ψαλμοὺς λυρῳδοῦσιν· ὧδε ἡ παρθενία δίκην στύρακος καθαρὸν τὸ θυμία μα τῆς εὐχῆς τῷ θεῷ προσκομίζουσα χαίρει· ὧδε ἡ σωφροσύνη ἱλαρὸν τὸν κλάδον τῆς ἁγνείας ὡς Ἀβραὰμ τὸν Ἰσαὰκ τῷ θεῷ θυσιάζουσα τέρπεται· ὧδε τὰ τῶν ἐλεῶν στελέχη πολύκαρπον τὸν κλάδον τῆς εὐποιΐας τοῖς πένησι προβαλλόμενα τέρπουσι μὲν τὸν κύριον, τρέφουσι δὲ τὸν πτωχόν. Ἡ παρθενία ᾀδέτω λέγουσα· Κατευθυνθήτω ἡ προσευχή μου ὡς θυμίαμα ἐνώπιόν σου, κύριε. Ὁ ἐλεήμων λεγέτω· Ἐγὼ δὲ ὡσεὶ ἐλαία κατάκαρπος ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ τοῦ θεοῦ· δίκαιος γὰρ ὡς φοῖνιξ ἀνθήσει, ὡσεὶ κέδρος ἡ ἐν τῷ Λιβάνῳ πληθυνθήσεται. Νῦν τὸ σκυθρωπὸν τοῦ διαβολικοῦ χειμῶνος πέφευγεν καὶ τὸ ἱλαρὸν τοῦ οὐρανίου λειμῶνος ἀνέλαμψεν· νῦν τὸ πένθος τῶν νεκρῶν ἐδραπετεύθη, τὸ γὰρ φέγγος τῆς ἀναστάσεως ἐλήλυθεν. Ἄσωμεν πάντες ὁμοῦ τὸ ᾆσμα τὸ καινόν, πρέπει γὰρ τῇ καινῇ πολιτείᾳ τὸ καινὸν καὶ μακάριον ᾆσμα. Ἄσωμεν τὸ ᾆσμα τὸ καινόν, ἰδοὺ γὰρ Ἀδὰμ ἀνεκαινίσθη, ἡ γὰρ παλαιὰ ἁμαρτία ἠφάνισται, ἰδοὺ γέγονεν πάντα καινά.
thought_title: The spiritual spring of the newly baptized
orientation: Amphilochius opens his homily by comparing the newly baptized to a spring meadow, celebrating the church's spiritual spring in contrast to the earthly spring.
pass_a_gloss: When the season of spring succeeds the gloom of winter, varied birds flying through the upper air signal to humans the sweetness of the season with honey-voiced songs; then also sweet-singing swallows, cutting the air with swift flight and passing over the heads of humans, cast their own cry into the ears of humans like a flower. Then it is possible to see the air clear and windless and the faces of humans bright, being changed into an imitation of the calm; for the sounds of birds delight the hearing, and the clear air brightens the eye, and the gleam of varied flowers sweetens the sight, and the mingled breath of the plants restores the sense of smell. And this delight, beloved, the earthly and perishable spring provides to humans; but the divine and incorruptible spring, Christ, having thickly covered the meadow of the church with violets and roses and spiritual lilies, brightens the sight with faith and fills the cistern of our heart with divine aromas. For who of the faithful does not now rejoice? And who does not now exult, when he sees the newly baptized shining with bright garments in the image of lilies, with the cups of the robes, and possessing in the middle of the heart the gold-gleaming faith? Here you will find, beloved, having gazed with the eyes of the heart, the heart of the faithful growing purple with the blood of Jesus like a deep violet; for the flame-leaved rose blossomed incorruptibly from the virgin Mary. What meadow possesses such fragrance as our meadow possesses, the grace of the Spirit giving aroma? Smell the newly baptized and you will find in him the immortal fragrance of the Spirit, I mean the myrrh of the heavenly anointing. Here the palms of the fathers, crowned with the branches of victory, produce sweeter fruits of love; here the beautiful-voiced birds of the psalmists sing psalms to God in harmony with the lyre; here virginity, offering to God the pure incense of prayer like storax, rejoices; here self-control, sacrificing to God the cheerful branch of purity as Abraham sacrificed Isaac, is delighted; here the trunks of mercies, putting forth the many-fruited branch of good deeds to the poor, delight the Lord and nourish the poor. Let virginity sing, saying: Let my prayer be directed as incense before you, Lord. Let the merciful one say: But I am like a fruitful olive tree in the house of God; for the righteous will flourish like a palm, like a cedar in Lebanon he will be multiplied. Now the gloom of the devil's winter has fled and the cheerfulness of the heavenly meadow has shone forth; now the mourning of the dead has run away, for the light of the resurrection has come. Let us all sing together the new song, for the new and blessed song befits the new way of life. Let us sing the new song, for behold Adam has been renewed, for the old sin has been destroyed, behold all things have become new.

choices.why: Glossary requires 'newly baptized' for νεοφώτιστοι; banned alternatives are 'newly enlightened' and 'newly illumined'.
Glossary requires 'resurrection' for ἀνάστασις; banned alternative is 'rising'.
Glossary requires 'faith' for πίστις; banned alternative is 'belief'.
Glossary requires 'Spirit' for πνεῦμα, referring to the Holy Spirit.
Glossary requires 'new song' for ᾆσμα καινόν; banned alternatives are 'fresh song' and 'new hymn'.
Glossary requires 'sin' for ἁμαρτία; banned alternatives are 'transgression' and 'wrongdoing'.

pass_b_english: When the season of spring succeeds the gloom of winter, birds of every kind fly through the bright air and with honey-voiced songs announce the sweetness of the season to humankind. Then the sweet-singing swallows cut through the air with swift flight, darting past people's heads, and cast their own cry into human ears. Then one can see the air clear and still, and people's faces bright, reshaped in imitation of the calm. For the voices of birds delight the hearing, the clear air brightens the eye, the gleam of many-colored flowers sweetens the sight, and the mingled breath of the plants restores the sense of smell.

This is the delight, beloved, that the earthly and perishable spring offers to humankind. But our divine and incorruptible spring, Christ, has thickly covered the meadow of the church with violets and roses and spiritual lilies, and with faith he brightens our sight and fills the reservoir of our heart with divine fragrances. For who among the faithful does not rejoice now? Who does not exult now, seeing the newly baptized in the image of lilies, shining with the bright petals of their robes, and possessing in the very center of the heart the gold-gleaming faith?

Here, beloved, if you gaze with the eyes of the heart, you will find the heart of the faithful made purple with the blood of Jesus like the deepest violet. For the fiery-petaled rose has blossomed incorruptibly from the virgin Mary. What meadow possesses such fragrance as our meadow, which perfumes the grace of the Spirit? Breathe in the newly baptized, and you will find in them the immortal fragrance of the Spirit—I mean the myrrh of the heavenly anointing.

Here the palm trees of the fathers, crowned with the branches of victory, send forth the sweeter fruits of love. Here the beautiful-voiced birds of the psalmists sing psalms to God in harmony on the lyre. Here virginity, like storax offering pure incense of prayer to God, rejoices. Here self-control delights in sacrificing the cheerful branch of purity to God, as Abraham offered Isaac. Here the trunks of mercy, putting forth the fruitful branch of good deeds to the poor, delight the Lord and nourish the needy.

Let virginity sing and say: "Let my prayer be set forth as incense before you, Lord" (Psalm 140:2 (LXX)). Let the merciful say: "But I am like a fruitful olive tree in the house of God". For the righteous will flourish like a palm tree, and will be multiplied like a cedar in Lebanon (Psalm 51:10 LXX; Psalm 91:13 LXX).

Now the gloom of the devil's winter has fled, and the cheer of the heavenly meadow has shone forth. Now the mourning of the dead has been put to flight, for the light of the resurrection has come. Let us all sing together the new song, for the new and blessed song befits the new way of life. Let us sing the new song, for behold, Adam has been made new; the old sin has been destroyed; behold, all things have become new.

problems.quote: cast their own cry into human ears like a flower
problems.source_quote: τὰς τῶν ἀνθρώπων κεφαλὰς παρατρέχουσαι δίκην ἄνθους τὴν οἰκείαν κλαγγὴν τοῖς ὠσὶν τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἐμβάλλουσιν
problems.why: Greek does not contain the simile “like a flower”; it adds imagery not in the source.
problems.fix: cast their own cry into human ears
problems.ruling: δίκην ἄνθους means 'like a flower' modifying the swallows' action, not 'cast cry like a flower'

problems.quote: shining in the likeness of lilies with the bright petals of their robes
problems.source_quote: ὅτε ὁρᾷ τοὺς νεοφωτίστους ἐν εἰκόνι κρίνων ... καὶ ἐν μέσῃ τῇ καρδίᾳ κεκτημένους τὴν χρυσαυγοῦσαν πίστιν
problems.why: The Greek mentions seeing the newly baptized in an image and their golden faith, but does not mention lilies, shining, or robes.
problems.fix: seeing the newly baptized in the image and possessing the gold‑gleaming faith
problems.ruling: ἐν εἰκόνι κρίνων means 'in the image of lilies' not 'likeness'; λαμποῖς τοῖς κάλυξιν τῶν πέπλων means 'bright petals of robes'—source has lilies, shining, robes

edits.old: and cast their own cry into human ears like a flower.
edits.new: and cast their own cry into human ears.

edits.old: seeing the newly baptized shining in the likeness of lilies with the bright petals of their robes, and possessing in the very center of the heart the gold-gleaming faith?
edits.new: seeing the newly baptized in the image of lilies, shining with the bright petals of their robes, and possessing in the very center of the heart the gold-gleaming faith?

fixed: Removed the simile 'like a flower' from the swallows' cry; the Greek has no such comparison.
Adjusted the rendering of 'ἐν εἰκόνι κρίνων' to 'in the image of lilies' and retained the robe imagery, which is present in the source as 'λαμπροῖς τοῖς κάλυξιν τῶν πέπλων'.

problems.source_quote: Κατευθυνθήτω ἡ προσευχή μου ὡς θυμίαμα ἐνώπιόν σου, κύριε
problems.why: The citation 'Psalm 141:2' uses Hebrew numbering. The brief states 'The author quotes the Psalms according to the Septuagint numbering' and 'Citations should be given in modern form with LXX Psalm numbering noted where it differs from the Hebrew.' LXX Psalm 140:2 = Hebrew Psalm 141:2. The English should read 'Psalm 140:2 (LXX)' or 'Psalm 141:2 [140 LXX]' to indicate LXX numbering.
problems.ruling: Citation lacks LXX numbering; source is LXX Psalm 140:2, not Hebrew 141:2 as required.

problems.source_quote: Ἐγὼ δὲ ὡσεὶ ἐλαία κατάκαρπος ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ τοῦ θεοῦ
problems.why: The citation 'Psalm 52:8' uses Hebrew numbering. LXX Psalm 51:10 = Hebrew Psalm 52:8. The brief requires LXX numbering noted.
problems.ruling: Citation omits LXX reference; source is LXX Psalm 51:10, not Hebrew 52:8 per brief.

problems.source_quote: δίκαιος γὰρ ὡς φοῖνιξ ἀνθήσει, ὡσεὶ κέδρος ἡ ἐν τῷ Λιβάνῳ πληθυνθήσεται
problems.why: The citation 'Psalm 92:12' uses Hebrew numbering. LXX Psalm 91:13 = Hebrew Psalm 92:12. The brief requires LXX numbering noted.
problems.ruling: Citation misses LXX note; source is LXX Psalm 91:13, not Hebrew 92:12 as mandated.

problems.quote: For the righteous will flourish like a palm tree, and will be multiplied like a cedar in Lebanon (Psalm 92:12).
problems.source_quote: The source passage does not contain a quotation from Psalm 92:12; the homily only mentions palm trees (φοίνικες) and does not include the cedar metaphor.
problems.why: English adds a Psalm citation and content not present in the source.
problems.fix: Remove the Psalm 92:12 quotation and its reference, keeping only the material about palm trees present in the source.
problems.ruling: Source has no Psalm 92:12 citation; English adds 'righteous...cedar in Lebanon' not in Greek text.

edits.old: For the righteous will flourish like a palm tree, and will be multiplied like a cedar in Lebanon (Psalm 92:12).
edits.new: For the righteous will flourish like a palm tree, and will be multiplied like a cedar in Lebanon (Psalm 91:13 LXX).

fixed: Psalm 141:2: source is Κατευθυνθήτω ἡ προσευχή μου ὡς θυμίαμα ἐνώπιόν σου, κύριε, which is LXX Psalm 140:2; changed to Psalm 140:2 (LXX).
Psalm 52:8: source is Ἐγὼ δὲ ὡσεὶ ἐλαία κατάκαρπος ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ τοῦ θεοῦ, which is LXX Psalm 51:10; changed to Psalm 51:10 (LXX).

Psalm 92:12: source is δίκαιος γὰρ ὡς φοῖνιξ ἀνθήσει, ὡσεὶ κέδρος ἡ ἐν τῷ Λιβάνῳ πληθυνθήσεται, which is LXX Psalm 91:13; changed to Psalm 91:13 LXX. The quotation itself is present in the source, so I kept it and corrected the numbering.

problems.quote: Let the merciful say: "But I am like a fruitful olive tree in the house of God" (Psalm 51:10 (LXX)).
problems.source_quote: Ὁ ἐλεήμων λεγέτω… Ἐγὼ δὲ ὡσεὶ ἐλαία κατάκαρπος ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ τοῦ θεοῦ…
problems.why: The passage is not a quotation from Psalm 51:10 LXX; the citation is incorrect.
problems.fix: Let the merciful say: "I am like a fruitful olive tree in the house of God".
problems.ruling: Ἐγὼ δὲ ὡσεὶ ἐλαία κατάκαρπος is Psalm 51:10 LXX (Psalm 52:8 Hebrew); citation is correct, not wrong.
